Implement formal verifier oracles (Header Space Analysis / NetPlumber-style checks) to evaluate reachability and policy properties. Evaluate three interventions: (1) base LLM generation (in-context prompting), (2) LLM with syntax-only repair pipeline, (3) agentic LLM with retrieval + formal verifier and iterative repair loop. For each scenario run N independent tasks per topology-size (paired assignment across interventions). Record raw model outputs, verifier logs, and final applied configurations. Preregister task sets, seeds, model versions, prompts, and retry policy before execution.","expected_data":"Per-task records including intervention identifier, model prompts/outputs, verifier pass/fail flags, list of detected semantic regressions, time-to-repair, number of repair iterations, and topology/vendor metadata. Aggregate metrics: repair success rate, semantic-regression rate, verifier-detected false negatives, average iterations to pass, and per-topology performance breakdowns.","primary_outcome":"Difference in semantic-regression rates (undetected or introduced regressions per 100 tasks) between base LLM and verifier-assisted agentic system, reported as paired effect size and 95% confidence interval across tasks and topology sizes.","analysis_outline":"Paired comparisons using Wilcoxon signed-rank test or paired t-test (after normality check) for regression rates between interventions; compute effect sizes (Cohen's d or matched-rank effect). Perform sensitivity analysis for prompt variants and perform multiple-comparison correction (Benjamini–Hochberg) across subgroups. Report task-level failure-mode taxonomy and qualitative examples.","novelty_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W7157506260","https://openalex.org/W4405229682"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W1882012874","https://openalex.org/W7163636922","https://openalex.org/W4404602270"],"risks":["Public configuration corpora may not fully capture vendor diversity, limiting external validity.","Formal verifiers require accurate network models; modeling mismatches could bias oracle judgments.","Benchmark creation may inadvertently introduce dataset contamination with model training data if public sources overlap with LLM corpora.","Compute and orchestration failures during large paired runs may force deviations from preregistered sample sizes."],"estimated_model_calls":3200},{"candidate_id":"adversarial-robustness-agentic-repair-2026","title":"Adversarial Robustness of Agentic Generate–Validate–Repair Loops in NetOps","research_question":"How robust are agentic generate–validate–repair NetOps workflows to adversarial or intentionally malformed configuration perturbations compared to base LLM repair pipelines?","hypotheses":["Agentic generate–validate–repair architectures will have lower overall semantic-regression rates under random faults but will remain vulnerable to adversarial perturbations crafted to evade the chosen formal verifiers.","Adversarial perturbations will cause a measurable increase in false‑validation events (changes that pass the oracle but produce operationally harmful outcomes) relative to non-adversarial cases.","Defense strategies that diversify verifier properties (e.g., multiple complementary oracles) will reduce adversarial success rates compared to single-oracle setups."],"proposed_design":"Create a controlled corpus of configuration faults including (a) random/synthetic misconfigurations and (b) adversarial perturbations designed to exploit known verifier modeling blind spots (e.g., ambiguous abstractions, header-space edge cases). For each fault, run each system and record whether the produced fix is applied, whether the verifier(s) accept it, and whether a secondary operational simulator (reachability plus sample traffic scenarios) indicates degraded operational metrics. Define adversary strategies algorithmically (targeted perturbations, gradient-free search over config edits) and limit total adversarial queries per task under preregistered budget. Compare adversarial success rates and false-validation frequencies across systems.","expected_data":"Per-case labels: fault type (random/adversarial), intervention, verifier outcomes (accept/reject), secondary-simulator operational verdicts (pass/fail), time and iterations to fix, and textual model outputs. must sanitize exploit details in outputs."],"estimated_model_calls":2600},{"candidate_id":"verifier-to-operational-impact-mapping-2026","title":"Mapping Formal-Verifier Outcomes to Operational Impact Metrics for LLM-driven NetOps","research_question":"Can outputs from formal verification tools (reachability/policy pass/fail) be quantitatively mapped to operational impact metrics (outage probability, rollback cost, mean-time-to-repair) for LLM-generated NetOps changes?","hypotheses":["A verifier pass correlates with reduced short-term outage probability and lower rollback cost on average, but the correlation is imperfect and varies by fault class and topology.","Some verifier-passed changes still cause nontrivial operational impacts detectable by simulated traffic/SLO models, indicating that verifier pass is a necessary but not sufficient predictor of low operational risk.","Combining verifier outcomes with lightweight operational simulation features (e.g., traffic sensitivity, path redundancy) yields a predictive model that outperforms verifier pass/fail alone for estimating outage risk."],"proposed_design":"Assemble a dataset of NetOps change attempts (LLM-generated or human-seeded) applied in simulated network environments parameterized with traffic matrices and SLOs. For each candidate change, run a formal verifier (reachability/policy checks) and an operational simulator that measures outage probability, rollback cost (estimated via simulated change fallout and automated rollback heuristics), and MTTR under injected failures. Collect verifier outputs, simulator-derived operational metrics, and auxiliary features (topology redundancy, affected prefix counts). Fit predictive models (logistic regression and random forest) to predict high operational-impact events using verifier outputs alone and combined feature sets. Evaluate calibration and discriminative performance on held-out tasks.","expected_data":"Per-change records: verifier pass/fail with detailed counterexamples (if fail), simulator outage probability, estimated rollback cost, MTTR, topology and traffic features. Train predictive models with cross-validation; report AUC-ROC, AUPRC, Brier score, and calibration for each model variant. Use permutation feature importance and SHAP-like summaries for interpretability. Conduct decision-curve analysis to estimate operational utility of using enhanced predictors for rollout gating.","novelty_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W2742515467","https://openalex.org/W7157506260","https://openalex.org/W7162218766"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W1882012874","https://openalex.org/W7162123183","https://openalex.org/W4404602270"],"risks":["Operational simulator abstractions (traffic models, SLO thresholds) may misrepresent real-world operator priorities, limiting external validity.","Predictive models may overfit to simulated scenarios and not generalize to unseen topologies or traffic patterns.","Estimating rollback cost requires assumptions about change propagation and operator intervention that may be site-specific."],"estimated_model_calls":1800},{"candidate_id":"benchmark-contamination-audit-netops-2026","title":"Audit of Data Contamination and Construct Validity in LLM-for-NetOps Benchmarks","research_question":"How prevalent are dataset contamination and construct-invalidity issues in existing LLM-for-NetOps benchmark suites, and how much do contamination controls affect reported model performance?","hypotheses":["A nontrivial fraction of existing benchmark tasks contain material overlap with public LLM training corpora, inflating reported performance.","Applying contamination controls (removing overlapping examples, using temporal splits, or augmenting with novel scenarios) will produce a statistically significant decrease in measured LLM performance on NetOps tasks.","Construct-invalid tasks (e.g., trivially templated prompts or unrealistic topologies) will show the largest performance drops under contamination control and realism adjustments.",""],"proposed_design":"Select a representative set of public NetOps/LLM benchmarks and datasets cited in the literature leads. For each dataset perform contamination heuristics: exact-match fingerprinting, fuzzy textual overlap, and metadata-based source tracing against known public corpora. Create contamination-controlled splits by removing or holding out overlapping items and generate realism-adjusted variants (e.g., multi-vendor retemplating, added topology complexity). Evaluate a set of LLMs and in-context prompting methods on original vs contamination-controlled datasets, measuring standard task metrics (accuracy, repair rate) and compute per-dataset performance deltas. Preregister contamination detection heuristics and thresholds, model versions, and evaluation prompts.","expected_data":"Per-dataset contamination rates (absolute and percent), model performance on original vs controlled splits, per-task performance deltas, and classification of tasks by construct-validity (templated vs realistic). Aggregate metrics: mean performance drop after contamination control, distribution of contamination across dataset sources.","primary_outcome":"Average relative drop in model performance (percentage points) across evaluated benchmarks after applying preregistered contamination controls, with 95% confidence intervals and task-level variance.","analysis_outline":"Estimate contamination prevalence with descriptive statistics. Compare per-model performance on original vs cleaned splits using paired tests (paired t-test/Wilcoxon). Report effect sizes and stratify by task construct class. Perform sensitivity analyses over contamination-detection thresholds and report false-positive risk of contamination heuristics. Document provenance traces for flagged items.","novelty_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W7166900660","https://openalex.org/W7140000903","https://openalex.org/W7157506260"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4404602270","https://openalex.org/W4404534210"],"risks":["Contamination detection heuristics can produce false positives/negatives; overly aggressive cleaning may remove valid evaluation items.","Access to authoritative LLM training-corpus manifests is limited, so overlap inferences remain probabilistic.","Audit results could be sensitive for dataset maintainers; disclosure requires careful, non-defamatory wording."],"estimated_model_calls":1200}]} for TypeAdapter(CandidateSet); 1 validation error for CandidateSet
